items.question: An order app's exchange rejects a position's stop-loss leg at activation because the price is already past the stop level (state rejected:price_too_high). The position now has no stop. What should the app do?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Alarm only: log, sound and page the owner.

options.label: (b)
options.text: Place a replacement reduce-only stop-market order.

options.label: (c)
options.text: Flatten the position at once with a reduce-only market order, and alarm.

items.rationale: A rejection for price_too_high means the stop level is already breached, so the stop would have fired: flattening does what the stop was for. (b) can be rejected again for the same reason in a fast market. (a) leaves an unprotected position while the owner may be asleep.

items.question: An order app's watchdog finds a live position with no stop order for more than 5 s, for a reason it cannot identify (for example the owner may have cancelled the stop by hand). What should it do?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Alarm only: log, sound and page urgently once per episode.

items.rationale: The cause is unknown and may be deliberate; flattening a position the owner meant to hold without a stop is an action the app cannot justify. The alarm reaches the owner.

items.question: An order app lets the owner set a stop only 5 USD from entry; in a fast market the stop is already crossed at activation and the exchange rejects it. A separate change will flatten the position when that happens. Should the app also enforce a minimum stop distance at placement?

options.label: (a)
options.text: No floor for now; the flatten-on-rejection change handles the crossed case.

options.label: (b)
options.text: Add a configurable minimum distance that refuses placements below it.

items.rationale: The owner tests with deliberately tight stops; the rejection handler makes a crossed stop safe. A floor can be added later if needed.

items.question: An order app's triggered stop-loss is already a resting reduce-only limit order chasing the top of the book every 333 ms to close the position. The owner presses a Reduce button, which sends a second reduce-only limit; the exchange rejects it (11030). What should Reduce do while a triggered stop is closing?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Refuse with a clear message: the triggered stop is already closing the position.

options.label: (b)
options.text: Cancel the stop first, then place the reduce limit.

options.label: (c)
options.text: Re-price the triggered stop to the reduce price.

items.rationale: The triggered stop is already as aggressive as a post-only order can be, and the chase would override (c) within 333 ms. (b) leaves the position with no stop while a limit rests. (a) is honest and changes nothing that protects the position.
